search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting West Nile virus cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and surveillance data for California during August 2024 (2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31), covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified cases, deaths, hospitalizations, subnational and local locations, and date reported.
search_reasoning: The upstream planned queries are a reasonable starting point but have several weaknesses that reduce their effectiveness in iteration 1: (1) They use overly rigid exact-phrase matching (e.g., "WNV California August 2024") that is unlikely to match real agency page titles or report language; (2) They embed the date range string "2024-08-01-2024-08-31" literally, which will not appear in natural-language source text; (3) They do not target the specific California Department of Public Health (CDPH) or county-level health department naming conventions used in WNV surveillance reports; (4) They do not leverage the CDC ArboNET system, which is the primary structured national WNV surveillance database and would cover California data; (5) They do not target CDPH's specific WNV weekly/annual statistical report pages. Given the 4-query cap for iteration 1, I prioritize: (A) CDPH official WNV surveillance page (highest authority, state-level, covers all counties); (B) CDC ArboNET / CDC WNV data for California 2024 (national structured database, cross-validates state data); (C) A targeted web search for county-level California WNV reports in August 2024 (captures sub-state granularity for locality field); (D) A news search for California WNV August 2024 deaths/cases (captures timely reporting and evidence quotes). Literature queries are deprioritized for iteration 1 because peer-reviewed publications on a specific one-month window in 2024 are unlikely to exist yet; they are better suited for iteration 2 if needed. The language is English only; no localization needed for California.

query_batch.query: California Department of Public Health West Nile virus 2024 cases deaths statistics site:cdph.ca.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: CDPH is the primary authoritative source for statewide WNV surveillance in California. Targeting the cdph.ca.gov domain directly maximizes the chance of retrieving the official 2024 WNV statistical report or weekly update page, which will contain confirmed/probable case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns. This is the highest-value query for all target fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH WNV surveillance statistics page or annual/weekly report PDF listing case counts by county and week for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official California state health agency domain (cdph.ca.gov); tabular case/death data with county breakdown

query_batch.query: CDC ArboNET West Nile virus California 2024 human cases deaths neuroinvasive site:cdc.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and the definitive structured database for WNV human case counts in the US, including California. The CDC WNV data page publishes state-level confirmed neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts and deaths by year. This cross-validates CDPH data and may provide case classification breakdowns (confirmed vs. probable) not always visible in state reports.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV data summary table or ArboNET report for 2024 with California row showing neuroinvasive/non-neuroinvasive cases and deaths
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official US federal health agency domain (cdc.gov); ArboNET system attribution; tabular state-level data

query_batch.query: West Nile virus California county August 2024 cases confirmed deaths public health department
query_batch.query_rationale: California WNV reporting is also conducted at the county level (e.g., Los Angeles County DPH, Sacramento County, Kern County), which are the primary sources for locality-level data. This broader web search targets county health department pages and press releases reporting WNV cases in August 2024, enabling population of the 'locality' field and capturing sub-state geographic granularity not always present in state-level summaries.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: County public health department press releases, advisories, or surveillance updates mentioning specific WNV case counts and deaths in August 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: County health department domain (e.g., publichealth.lacounty.gov, sacpublichealth.net, kernpublichealth.com); official press release format with case counts

query_batch.query: West Nile virus California August 2024 death cases reported outbreak
query_batch.query_rationale: News sources often report WNV deaths and case milestones in near-real-time, citing official health department figures. A news search for August 2024 California WNV activity will surface evidence quotes, specific dates of reporting, and locality names that can be cross-referenced against official sources. This is especially valuable for the 'evidence_quote' and 'date_reported' fields and for identifying which counties had notable activity during the target window.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News articles from regional California outlets (e.g., Sacramento Bee, LA Times, Fresno Bee) or wire services (AP, Reuters) reporting WNV cases or deaths in California in August 2024, citing health department data
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Dateline within August 2024; explicit citation of CDPH or county health department figures; named journalist byline

language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. California WNV surveillance is conducted entirely in English by CDPH and county health departments. No Spanish-language or other localization is needed for official surveillance data, though Spanish-language news sources could be considered in iteration 2 if county-level locality coverage is insufficient for communities in the Central Valley or Southern California.
trust_considerations: Highest trust: CDPH (cdph.ca.gov) and CDC (cdc.gov) official surveillance pages — these are primary authoritative sources for case counts and deaths
High trust: California county health department official websites (.gov or recognized county domains) with dated press releases
Moderate trust: Regional news articles that explicitly cite CDPH or county health department figures with named sources
Lower trust: General web pages, blogs, or aggregator sites without clear attribution to official health agency data — use only for evidence quotes pointing back to official sources
Note: CDC ArboNET data for 2024 may be preliminary and subject to revision; CDPH data should be treated as the primary California-specific source
Exact-phrase queries with literal date strings (e.g., '2024-08-01-2024-08-31') are unlikely to match real source text and have been replaced with natural-language time terms
stop_condition_hypothesis: Sufficient evidence coverage is achieved when at least one CDPH or CDC official source is identified with case counts and at least one county-level or news source provides locality-level granularity and evidence quotes for the August 2024 window. If iteration 1 returns strong CDPH and CDC hits with case/death counts, iteration 2 may only need county-level follow-up queries.

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong candidate sources from cdph.ca.gov (8 results) and cdc.gov (7 results), including a highly relevant CDPH news release (NR24-27) mentioning "63 human cases of West Nile virus, including six deaths" for 2024, and a CDPH 2024 year-end monthly summary PDF with WNV case breakdowns by type (neuroinvasive, non-neuroinvasive, asymptomatic). However, critical gaps remain for the August 2024 specific window: (1) The CDPH news release snippet does not confirm it is dated within August 2024 — it may be from a different point in the season; (2) The year-end PDF provides monthly columns but the snippet does not confirm which months are represented or whether August-specific counts are extractable; (3) The westnile.ca.gov domain (2 results) — the dedicated California WNV surveillance portal — was returned but not summarized, and it is the primary real-time WNV data source for California with weekly updates; (4) County-level locality data (ph.lacounty.gov, nevadacountyca.gov, lacounty.gov) appeared but were not summarized; (5) The CDC ArboNET historic data page was returned but only as a navigation/landing page — the actual 2024 state-level data table for California has not been confirmed; (6) No August-specific weekly WNV report from CDPH or westnile.ca.gov has been confirmed in the snippets. Iteration 2 should target: (A) westnile.ca.gov directly for weekly/cumulative 2024 WNV statistics; (B) CDPH news release NR24-27 context and date confirmation via a targeted search; (C) County-level August 2024 WNV reports for high-burden counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno); (D) CDC WNV 2024 current season data page (distinct from historic data). This is the final allowed iteration (max_iterations=2), so queries must be maximally targeted.

This is the highest-value source for August 2024 weekly case counts and county-level locality data, and must be targeted directly in the final iteration.

query_batch.query: CDC West Nile virus 2024 current season data California cases neuroinvasive non-neuroinvasive site:cdc.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: The CDC ArboNET historic data page was returned in iteration 1 but only as a navigation/landing page. This page would provide federal-level cross-validation of California case counts for August 2024 and may include neuroinvasive/non-neuroinvasive breakdowns. Targeting cdc.gov with current-season terminology distinguishes this from the historic data page already returned.
